responsibilities: Own unit economics — build and maintain cost-to-serve, gross margin, and contribution models by product, customer, and workload, rebuilt from source data rather than spreadsheets.
Own budgeting for the technology organization: cloud and GPU/TPU spend attribution, vendor and capacity forecasting, and the models engineering leadership uses to plan.
Build and run finance dashboarding — a single source of truth for burn, runway, margin, and company KPIs that the leadership team and board can trust.
Automate budget-vs-actuals: live department-level views and overspend alerts that make budget and margin targets enforceable without manual chasing.

Build the deal desk framework: pricing and discount guardrails derived from the margin model, automated quote and order-form generation, and routing so only non-standard deals need escalation — raising deal throughput without finance in the loop on every deal.
Automate sales compensation: implement a comp tool and the pipelines behind it so statements, accelerators, and disputes run from CRM and billing data instead of spreadsheets.
Design and ship finance agents and internal tools — workflows that pull, reconcile, and summarize financial data so non-engineers get answers without filing a ticket.
Build and maintain the finance data layer: pipelines from billing, payroll, cloud, and accounting systems into a well-modeled warehouse.
Partner with the VP Finance, Controller, and engineering leadership to trace discrepancies to their real source and ship fixes that hold.

evidence.velocity_vs_rigour: you stay skeptical of your own results until they reconcile, and you treat an unexplained variance as a problem rather than noise
evidence.velocity_vs_rigour_explanation: Reconciliation and trust language ("a trusted number", "stay skeptical of your own results until they reconcile", "fixes that hold") outweighs the single "move fast" in the company intro, so rigour.
evidence.domain_risk: a single source of truth for burn, runway, margin, and company KPIs that the leadership team and board can trust
evidence.domain_risk_explanation: The role builds board-level financial reporting ("burn, runway, margin") and works with the Controller up to "quarter close", which is explicit financial reporting language.
evidence.collaboration_width: VP Finance; Controller; sales leadership; engineering and infrastructure leadership; board
evidence.data_team_maturity: Build and maintain the finance data layer: pipelines from billing, payroll, cloud, and accounting systems into a well-modeled warehouse.
evidence.data_team_maturity_explanation: The finance data layer, deal desk framework and comp tooling are still to be built, replacing spreadsheets ("rebuilt from source data rather than spreadsheets"), so the finance data function is early.
evidence.jd_authorship: cloud and GPU/TPU spend attribution, vendor and capacity forecasting, and the models engineering leadership uses to plan.
evidence.jd_authorship_explanation: Bullets name concrete models and systems ("cost-to-serve, gross margin, and contribution models", "GPU/TPU spend attribution"), so a reader knows the Tuesday-morning work.
evidence.stakeholder_orientation: The role is embedded within the Finance team and reports to the VP Finance.
evidence.stakeholder_orientation_explanation: The primary audience is the finance function ("embedded within the Finance team"), with unit economics, budget-vs-actuals and board KPIs as the core outputs.
evidence.autonomy_level_explanation: The role owns whole domains ("Own unit economics", "Own budgeting for the technology organization") and designs frameworks rather than receiving scoped work.
evidence.ai_role: Design and ship finance agents and internal tools — workflows that pull, reconcile, and summarize financial data so non-engineers get answers without filing a ticket.
evidence.ai_role_explanation: The candidate builds LLM-based finance agents that run on the finance data layer ("Design and ship finance agents"), so AI sits downstream of their output.
evidence.testing_framing: Partner with the VP Finance, Controller, and engineering leadership to trace discrepancies to their real source and ship fixes that hold.
evidence.testing_framing_explanation: Data correctness is an owned responsibility ("trace discrepancies to their real source and ship fixes that hold", "stay skeptical of your own results until they reconcile"), though no testing tool is named.
evidence.loss_aversion_framing: how quickly anyone here can get a trusted number on unit economics, cash burn, or technology spend and act on it
evidence.loss_aversion_framing_explanation: Trust in the numbers is the role summary's central framing ("a trusted number", "the leadership team and board can trust"), reflecting fear of wrong numbers reaching decision-makers.
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix_explanation: Most infrastructure verbs are "Build" and "implement" for systems that do not yet exist (deal desk framework, comp tool, finance data layer).
evidence.loss_aversion: The bar is someone who understands the decision a number is meant to support, measures it from the outset, and would rather find out a model was wrong in a week than at quarter close.
